A merge operation reports 'merge produced no new commits; verify the worker branch'. Initial hypothesis: the worker branch contains no useful commit.
The raw pre-merge result is ok=false, state=failed, commit_point=not_reached, error='target working tree is dirty (1 file: docs/tasks/49/)'. No merge attempt reached Git.

normalize_merge_result rewrites the raw dict whenever target ref is unchanged and commits_merged=0. That success-shaped predicate ignores the explicit failed state and replaces the useful raw error with the generic no-commits text.
After cleaning the target checkout, the same worker branch merges one commit. Reject the 'empty or unhealthy worker branch' hypothesis; the branch was healthy and target dirt caused the refusal.
Accepted minimal fix: use raw.get('error') when non-empty, otherwise fall back to the generic no-commits message. Preserve the existing typed error code as well as the specific message.
Acceptance must reject a half-fix that returns the dirty-target message under the wrong status/error code. The wrapper may add a code but may not replace the cause.
FINAL: return the owner, causal defect, minimal fix, fields that must be preserved, and the branch-health conclusion.
